faq.q: Do I need experience in support?
faq.a: No. The course starts from the basics, with examples from small businesses.

faq.q: Which help-desk software do I need?
faq.a: None. The labs run in your browser, and the concepts apply to any ticketing tool.
No. It builds practical skills and earns a completion badge on this platform, not an external accreditation.

activities.title: Write a reply to an unhappy customer
activities.objective: Write a reply that acknowledges, apologises sincerely, solves and follows up.
activities.scenario: A customer writes: 'I was charged twice for my monthly plan. I need this fixed today. This is the second time!' Write the reply from the support agent.
steps: Start with a greeting (Hello or Dear).
Acknowledge the problem and apologise once, specifically.
State exactly what you will do (refund the duplicate charge) and when.
Explain the next step the customer should expect.
Close with a follow-up promise and your name.
Keep it between 70 and 160 words.

checks.label: Names the problem
checks.hint: Mention the double charge or twice.
checks.explain: Specifics show you read the message.

checks.label: Gives a time
checks.hint: State when, such as today or within 24 hours.

checks.label: A follow-up promise
checks.hint: Say you will confirm or follow up.

activities.title: Measure response times and SLA
activities.objective: Calculate first response times, check them against a service-level target and summarise.
activities.scenario: A support team promises a first reply within 4 hours. Check ten tickets.
steps: In D2 show Met if the first response time (hours) is at most the target in B13, otherwise Missed; fill down to D11.
In B14 count the tickets that met the target with COUNTIF.
In B15 work out the SLA percentage: met divided by total tickets.
In B16 work out the average first response time with AVERAGE.
In B17 find the slowest response with MAX.
In B18 show On target if the SLA percentage is at least the goal in B19, otherwise Improve.

checks.label: D2 is Met for T-101
checks.explain: Compare the time with the target.

checks.label: B14 counts Met
checks.explain: Count the tickets that hit the target.

activities.title: Churn, retention and revenue
activities.objective: Calculate monthly churn, retention and lost revenue, and estimate customer lifetime.
activities.scenario: A subscription product started the month with 400 customers, lost 20 and won 30. Each pays 1,500 rupees a month.
steps: In B6 work out the customers at the end: start minus lost plus new.
In B7 work out the churn rate: lost divided by start.
In B8 work out the retention rate: 1 minus churn.
In B9 work out the monthly revenue lost to churn: lost customers times the price.
In B10 estimate the average customer lifetime in months: 1 divided by churn.
In B11 estimate lifetime revenue per customer: lifetime months times the price.

checks.label: B6 is customers at the end
B10 is lifetime in months
checks.hint: One divided by the churn rate.

activities.title: Build a customer health score
activities.objective: Combine usage, satisfaction and support signals into a health score to find customers at risk.
activities.scenario: Score each customer from 0 to 100 on usage (50%), satisfaction (30%) and tickets (20%, where fewer tickets is better). Label them.
steps: In E2 work out the health score: 0.5 times usage plus 0.3 times satisfaction plus 0.2 times the ticket score. Fill down to E6.
In F2 show Healthy if the score is at least 70, At risk if at least 50, otherwise Critical (nested IF). Fill down.
In B8 count the customers At risk or Critical: total customers minus Healthy, using COUNTIF.
In B9 find the lowest score with MIN.

activities.title: Calculate NPS and CSAT
activities.objective: Calculate Net Promoter Score and satisfaction from survey scores.
activities.scenario: Twenty customers answered 'How likely are you to recommend us (0-10)?'. Scores 9-10 are promoters, 7-8 passives, 0-6 detractors. Also, 25 people rated a support chat 1-5 and 4-5 counts as satisfied.
steps: In B5 count the promoters with COUNTIF on the scores (9 or more).
In B6 count the detractors (6 or less).
In B7 work out the percentage of promoters and in B8 the percentage of detractors (of 20).
In B9 work out NPS: percentage promoters minus percentage detractors, times 100.
In B12 work out CSAT: satisfied ratings divided by total ratings (input in B10 and B11).

activities.title: Write a voice-of-the-customer summary
activities.objective: Turn raw comments into themes and recommendations.
activities.scenario: You read 40 customer comments last month. Eleven mentioned slow replies, nine mentioned confusing set-up, six praised the friendly agents, and four asked for a mobile app. Summarise them.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: Summary, Top themes, Recommendations.
In Top themes list the themes with their counts in a bulleted list.
In Recommendations write a numbered list of at least three actions, each linked to a theme.
Keep it between 90 and 240 words.

activities.title: Final project: a customer success plan
activities.objective: Write a plan to onboard, support and retain customers with measures and actions.
activities.scenario: Write a one-page customer success plan for a small company selling accounting software to shops.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Customer success plan'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Goals, Onboarding, Support standards, Health and risks, Feedback, Measures.
Give goals with numbers such as churn or SLA targets.
Under Support standards state a response time target.
Under Measures list at least four indicators in a bulleted list.
Keep it between 180 and 400 words.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Goals, Onboarding, Support standards, Health and risks, Feedback, Measures.

checks.label: A response time
checks.hint: State a first-response target such as 4 hours.

checks.label: Uses course terms
checks.hint: Mention churn, NPS, CSAT or health score.
